newsitem.title: USA: Ford's Ford Division sees record 1996 sales.
newsitem.headline: Ford's Ford Division sees record 1996 sales.

text.p: Ford Motor Co's Ford Division is estimated to have sold 3,292,000 cars and light trucks in 1996, an increase of 30,000 from 1995 and a new record for the division, Division General Manager Ross Roberts said Monday.
The division believes its U.S. light truck market share rose and its car market share fell in 1996, Roberts said.
Light trucks will make up about 60 percent of the division's 1996 sales, up from 57-58 percent in 1995, he said.
Ford is to report its December and full-year 1996 sales later today.

Roberts said he expects rebates to continue in the auto industry, in part because of excess worldwide capacity. He said the global industry has excess production capacity of about eight million vehicles, most of that on the passenger car side.
Roberts expects the pickup truck and sport/utility segments to continue strong, at the expense of minivans and passenger cars.
Ford today introduced its new Escort ZX2, a sport coupe aimed at young buyers, more than half which are expected to be women, according to Roberts.
Annual production of the vehicle is expected to be 75,000. The car will be built in Hermosillo, Mexico.
Prices have not been set but will be similar to those of the Escort compact car, Roberts said.

Production of the ZX2, a 1998 model year car, starts February 17. The car, slated to go on sale April 17, is built from a derivative of the Escort platform. It features a 130-horsepower, 16-valve engine with a dual overhead camshaft.
Median age for a coupe buyer is expected to be 32, and median income $42,000, against 39 and $33,000, respectively, for the Escort sedan buyer.
